name: Vast.ai GPU marketplace (supply-and-demand, interruptible-first)
price_basis: NO price_usd recorded on purpose. Vast is a marketplace: 'prices set by supply and demand across 40+ data centers' and 'you always see the real rate'. The Live GPU Prices grid renders client-side from an API and carried no numbers in the extracted HTML on 2026-10-03, so any figure I wrote would be a guess dressed as data. The one QUANTIFIED statement on the page is a discount ceiling: Interruptible is '50%+ cheaper' than on-demand, and Reserved is 'Up to 50% Off'.
notes: A structural record, and the cheapest credible ROUTE to consumer and workstation NVIDIA silicon - the right provider for an RTX 4090/5090 hour or an L40S, and the wrong one for an H100 with guaranteed capacity. Three structural facts from the page: 68+ GPU types, per-second billing with 'no minimum hours, no rounding up', and three tiers - On-Demand (guaranteed uptime, no interruptions, per-second), Interruptible ('Best Value', '50%+ cheaper', 'preemptible - may be reclaimed', for batch training), and Reserved (1/3/6-month terms, guaranteed capacity, up to 50% off, volume discounts, contact sales). The trust tradeoff is the whole story: the hosts are third parties, the supply varies minute to minute, and the page sells on the word 'transparency'. Do not confuse the 'Up to 50% Off' reserved ceiling with the '50%+ cheaper' interruptible tier - they are different mechanisms. If you need an interruptible price for H100 and Vast's grid is reachable to you, this is likely the floor of the entire market.
